business_description: Freelance graphic design and marketing consultancy
customer_behaviour: Customer received three payments from separate limited companies within a 6-day window. All three companies were incorporated within the last 18 months and show no trading history, no web presence, and minimal accounts filed at Companies House. Each payment was described as a 'consultancy retainer' with no supporting contract or statement of work provided when requested. All three payments cleared within 24 hours of being raised on invoice. Following receipt of funds, the customer made a series of outbound transfers to three different personal accounts held at different banks, and one transfer to a cryptocurrency exchange, within 48 hours.
analyst_notes: Customer contacted and asked to explain the nature of services rendered. Customer stated the work involved 'brand strategy and digital marketing' but was unable to name any deliverables, project timelines, or client contacts at the counterparty companies. All three counterparty companies share the same registered address in London EC2. Recommend SAR filing under NCA typology NCA-001 (Invoice Fraud). Account should be placed under enhanced monitoring pending investigation outcome.

customer_behaviour: Account received an inbound transfer of £31,000 from a victim's personal account at a different institution. The sending bank has contacted Lloyds to flag this as a reported APP scam. The victim states they were deceived by a fraudster posing as a Lloyds fraud prevention officer, who instructed them to move funds to a 'safe account' which turned out to be this account. Within 6 hours of receipt, the account holder made three outbound transfers: £12,000 to an account at Monzo, £10,500 to an account at Revolut, and £8,200 to a cryptocurrency exchange. The account holder has not responded to outreach from the bank.
analyst_notes: This is a confirmed receiving-side APP scam. The victim has filed a complaint with their own bank. Under the PSR Mandatory Reimbursement Scheme this account is subject to a 5-business-day response requirement. The account has been suspended. A SAR must be filed as a matter of urgency. The onward transfers to Monzo and Revolut have been reported via the Confirmation of Payee alerts network. The crypto exchange transfer has been flagged with the exchange's financial crime team.

customer_behaviour: This is the second structuring alert for this customer in the same period. Customer has made a total of four cash deposits across three branches in three days: £9,800 on 01 March (Branch: Manchester Piccadilly), £4,200 on 02 March (Branch: Manchester Deansgate), £5,400 on 02 March (Branch: Salford), and £9,600 on 03 March (Branch: Manchester Piccadilly). All deposits are in cash. Total cumulative cash deposits over the 3-day period: £29,000. The customer's stated occupation is a part-time retail assistant with a monthly salary of approximately £1,400. There is no plausible legitimate source for this volume and frequency of cash deposits. The branch pattern and sub-threshold amounts are consistent with a deliberate structuring strategy to avoid automated transaction monitoring triggers.
analyst_notes: Previous structuring alert ALT-00001 filed 2 days prior for same customer. Combined deposits now total £19,400 across two alerts in 3 days. Customer's income is wholly inconsistent with this level of cash activity. Pattern of sub-£10,000 deposits at multiple branches is textbook structuring behaviour. A SAR must be filed under POCA 2002. The account should be suspended pending MLRO review. Note: prior alert ALT-00001 is currently UNDER_REVIEW with analyst j.rahman.
